text: In spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), with delta_t = t_post - t_pre, when is a synapse potentiated (LTP)?
choices: When delta_t > 0 (presynaptic spike before postsynaptic): the input helps cause the post-spike, so the synapse strengthens
When delta_t < 0 (post before pre): the synapse strengthens
Whenever pre and post both fire, regardless of order
explanation: STDP is causal Hebbian: delta_w = +A_+*exp(-delta_t/tau_+) for delta_t > 0 (pre before post, LTP), and depression for delta_t < 0 (post before pre, LTD). Option 1 has the sign reversed, option 2 ignores the timing/causality that defines STDP, and potentiation is strongest as delta_t approaches 0 from above but is not confined to exactly zero.
